name: Maharashtrian Wada
planning_philosophy: Inward-looking family house of the Deccan: rooms and verandahs gather round a central open court (chowk / angan), with a raised entrance platform (otta), a public front and private rear, and timber, stone and clay as the main materials.
kitchen_planning: practical kitchen separated from the public rooms, connected to dining and to a utility / wash area
entrance_characteristics: raised otta with carved teak columns, a large double-leaf carved timber door under a tiled eave
material_appearance_hints: carved teak, stone flooring, clay roof tiles, lime-washed ochre, cream and muted-red walls, brass lanterns and jali screens
